newsitem.title: ALBANIA: SOCCER-ALBANIANS RESTART LEAGUE AFTER WEEK OF MIXED FORTUNES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ALBANIANS RESTART LEAGUE AFTER WEEK OF MIXED FORTUNES.

text.p: The Albanian soccer federation said on Monday it planned to restart the stalled national league in May by staging it in a few towns under police control.

Gjergj Thaka, a senior soccer federation official, said the remaining 17 rounds of the 18-team championship, which was suspended in January, would be held in Tirana, Elbasan and Kavaje and other towns in central Albania willing to offer stadiums.

Last week Albania were forced to play their World Cup match against Germany in the Spanish town of Granada because of the civil unrest at home. They surprised everyone by leading the European champions before going down 3-2.
The following day 12 of the under-21 team sought political asylum in Spain.
Thaka said teams from more lawless parts of the Balkan country would travel to the towns for league games.
"The championship cannot continue as before as there is no time and police cannot guarantee order...(but) we shall continue it in another form," Thaka said.

"The championship is of great influence and we are determined to hold it. Besides, we should continue to take part in the European Cups which are of great importance psychologically and financially for our clubs."
The federation was asking the state to unfreeze a blocked $240,000 fund to finance the league championship.
The semifinals of Albania's Cup would be held in Tirana if the four clubs involved approved.
There was also an upbeat tone to the loss of 12 of the 19 under-21 players.
"It was not a clandestine fleeing like after the collapse of communism in 1991," Sulejman Mema, under-21 coach, said.
The soccer officials said players did not consider themselves political refugees and would return to Albania if no team was interested in them.
